key_insight: ProIQA assesses generated math items by modeling not just the question stem, but the underlying solution process, enabling finer-grained quality evaluation across knowledge, difficulty, and competencies.
engineering_relevance: This provides a scalable, data-driven QA layer for automatic item generation systems in intelligent education, where manual review is too slow and shallow text-only checks miss reasoning quality.
method: Builds a process-enhanced IQA dataset by augmenting items with structured reasoning trees extracted from raw solutions.
Uses large language models to construct hierarchical reasoning trees and graph neural networks to encode their topology and procedural semantics.
Fuses stem semantics and solving-process representations in a dual-view "Stem + Solving" framework.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports extensive experiments on K12 math datasets, showing the approach captures process-oriented features for evaluating AIG outputs.
watch_item: Performance may depend on the quality of generated reasoning trees, so noisy LLM-derived process structures could affect assessment reliability.
paper_title: ProIQA: A Process-Based Framework for Fine-Grained Math Item Quality Assessment
